coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Edwin M. Lee Apartments (Block 3 East)
record.summary: Edwin M. Lee Apartments, an affordable multifamily building at 1150 Third Street on Mission Bay South Block 3 East: a five-story building with offices, a garage and a community room, sponsored by the Chinatown Community Development Center with Swords to Plowshares. The city permit was filed in December 2016 and marked complete on June 17, 2020; the Examiner reported that it had housed residents since February (2021) and that the grand opening was held in May 2021. Sources give 119 total units and 118 affordable units; the 62 veterans' and 56 or 57 family units are counted differently (see the unit-count note).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is the union of Assessor lots 8711026A and 8711026B (4,377 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed an idealized rectangle constructed by Pier & Point (no building footprint was available); 93% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 99% of the lot. The building it stands for is identified by DataSF's address point for 1150 3rd St, which lies inside the outline; the outline is the parcel that address point sits on (8711026), not the building's own footprint.

open_questions: Does the outline match the building's real footprint? The outline is now the parcel the address point sits on, which can include yard or plaza around the building; no source read gives the building's own footprint.

Unit count: OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report lists 119 total units and 118 affordable units, and the permit and Swords to Plowshares give 119; the Examiner and the Chinatown Community Development Center page say 118 (62 veteran plus 56 family units); SF YIMBY gives 118; SFBay (2018) says 'a total of 119 affordable units, 62 for homeless veterans, and 56 for low-income families', which sums to 118; Swords to Plowshares says 62 veterans and 57 families (119). Which family-unit count (56 or 57) is right, and what the one unit between 118 affordable and 119 total is (the source reports do not say; it may be a manager's unit), is not established.
Square footage differs: SF YIMBY gives 123,700 and the Chinatown Community Development Center page gives 81,295; not reconciled, so neither is recorded as a fact.

The exact move-in date is not stated: the Examiner (May 2021) says residents since 'February' without naming the year, and the permit shows completion in June 2020. The 2020-06-17 milestone is the permit's own completion date, not an occupancy date.
No OCII Commission document or press release for the opening was read as text; the primary-source figures come from OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report and the city permit data.
Final construction cost was not found; the $73,040,010 is a 2016 projection and the $45,000,000 is the permit's own estimate.

Unit count, source wording: OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report reads 'Total Units 119' and 'Total Affordable Units 118'; the permit describes '119 dwelling' units; the Examiner (May 2021) and the Chinatown Community Development Center page say 118 ('62 units designated for formerly homeless veterans and 56 units for low-income families'); Swords to Plowshares lists 62 veterans and 57 low-income families.
